name: The Person and Deity of the Holy Spirit
path: Pneumatology: The Doctrine of the Holy Spirit

objectives.text: Identify the Holy Spirit as God along with the Father and the Son
Name actions the Holy Spirit does in the Bible, such as teaching and helping, that show He is a Person and not a force
Recall from Ephesians 4:30 that the Holy Spirit can be grieved, which shows He is a Person and not a thing
Describe how the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are each present at the baptism of Jesus
Explain that the Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Trinity, distinct from the Father and the Son yet one God with them
Explain from Acts 5:3-4 why Peter treats lying to the Holy Spirit as lying to God
Explain why the church speaks of the Holy Spirit as He rather than it, using the personal language Jesus uses for the Spirit in John
Compare the personal acts Scripture ascribes to the Spirit, such as teaching, willing, and interceding, with the behavior of an impersonal force
Classify the divine attributes Scripture ascribes to the Spirit, such as eternity, omnipresence, and omniscience, with a supporting passage for each
Analyze how Acts 5:3-4 and 1 Corinthians 2:10-11 each establish the deity of the Holy Spirit
Analyze how the New Testament applies Old Testament words of the LORD to the Holy Spirit as evidence of His deity
Analyze the single divine name in the baptismal formula and the threefold apostolic benediction as evidence that the Spirit shares the Godhead equally with the Father and the Son
Explain the Reformed confession that the Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father and the Son, using John 15:26 and the confessional statements
Explain why the Nicene Creed confesses the Spirit as the Lord and giver of life who with the Father and the Son is worshiped and glorified, in light of the fourth-century denial of His deity
Distinguish the eternal procession of the Spirit within the Godhead from His sending by the Father and the Son at Pentecost
Construct a scriptural defense of the deity of the Holy Spirit drawing on the names, attributes, works, and worship Scripture gives Him
Evaluate the claim that the Holy Spirit is an impersonal power, as taught by groups such as the Jehovah's Witnesses, using the biblical evidence for His personhood
Evaluate modalism and subordinationism as errors about the Holy Spirit by comparing them with Scripture and the Reformed confessions
Compose a written synthesis of the biblical and confessional teaching that the Holy Spirit is a distinct Person and true, coeternal God with the Father and the Son

changes: Fixed the malformed reference to John 15:26 and checked all references for proper Book chapter:verse spacing. Kept and reworded the real competencies from the old list. Moved the Spirit as third Person from bare summary to a statement of distinction within unity. Added objectives on personal pronouns in John, Old Testament texts applied to the Spirit, the Nicene Creed's confession of the Spirit's worship in historical context, and the distinction between eternal procession and the Pentecost sending. Replaced the vague worship objective with the creedal one, and made the grade 12 synthesis a written product. Anchored doctrines to WSC Q6, WLC Q10-11, WCF 2.3, Heidelberg Q53, and Belgic Confession Article 11. Left the Spirit's work in creation, regeneration, sanctification, and gifts to the sibling sub-topics.
